_meta.indication: ZULRESSO is indicated for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD) in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing brexanolone 90 µg/kg/h and 60 µg/kg/h to placebo, administered as a 60-hour IV infusion
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HAM-D total score at 60 hours (end of infusion)
pivotal_trials.result: At Hour 60, placebo-subtracted difference in HAM-D change for 90 µg/kg/h was -3.7 (95% CI -6.9, -0.5; p=0.02) and for 60 µg/kg/h was -5.5 (95% CI -8.8, -2.2; p=0.0013)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of brexanolone 90 µg/kg/h vs placebo as a 60-hour IV infusion
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with moderate PPD (baseline HAM-D 20 to 25)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HAM-D total score at 60 hours
pivotal_trials.result: At Hour 60, placebo-subtracted difference in HAM-D change was -2.5 (95% CI -4.5, -0.5; p=0.0160), statistically significant after MCP adjustment

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and at least twice the rate of placebo) were sedation/somnolence, dry mouth, loss of consciousness, and flushing/hot flush. At the 90 µg/kg/hour dose sedation/somnolence occurred in 13% (vs 6% placebo), loss of consciousness in 3%, and flushing/hot flush in 2%
target_moa: Brexanolone is chemically identical to the endogenous hormone allopregnanolone and appears to act as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA_A receptors

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EXCESSIVE SEDATION AND SUDDEN LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS — patients are at risk of excessive sedation or sudden loss of consciousness during administration and must be monitored with continuous pulse oximetry; ZULRESSO is available only through the ZULRESSO REMS

rems.type: ZULRESSO is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the ZULRESSO REMS because excessive sedation or sudden loss of consciousness can result in serious harm; healthcare facilities and pharmacies must be enrolled/certified

advisory_committee.vote: A joint meeting of the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee and Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee was held November 2, 2018; the committee voted 18-0 that substantial evidence supported effectiveness, and 17-1 that benefits outweigh the risks when used in a certified facility under the proposed REMS

description.text: Expanded indication for postpartum depression to include patients 15 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for expansion of the indication to include patients 15 years and older diagnosed with postpartum depression and addition of corresponding study information to applicable sections of the package insert, medication guide, and REMS.

basis.text: Granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on August 23, 2016 for treatment of PPD, based on an open-label study terminated early for efficacy and a phase 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (547-PPD-202A)

citations.quote: Brexanolone was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on August 23, 2016 for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD). The Breakthrough Therapy designation was based on the results of an open-label study (terminated early for efficacy after four patients had a large response) and a phase 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (Study 547-PPD-202A).

summary.text: Brexanolone (Zulresso) was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on August 23, 2016 for PPD and received Priority review; approval was supported by two positive adequate and well-controlled trials and was based on standard (not accelerated) approval. It was approved with a boxed warning and a REMS.

citations.quote: Brexanolone was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on August 23, 2016 for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD).
